name: YouCanBookMe
tagline: Offer booking pages with availability rules, confirmations, and rescheduling

pricing.hiddenCosts: Added seats are prorated; Stripe/payment fees remain separate; UK customers may owe 20% VAT.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For YouCanBookMe, offer booking pages with availability rules, confirmations, and rescheduling. The hard boundary is calendar integration maturity, forms, reminders, payments, and support, plus calendar integrations and reliability.
coreLoopDIY: Read one calendar, publish booking pages with availability rules, create conflict-safe bookings, support rescheduling, and send confirmations and reminders.
whatYouLose: calendar integration maturity, forms, reminders, payments, and support
ongoingBurden: OAuth refresh, webhooks, timezone databases, race conditions, reminders, deliverability, privacy, and uptime
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for YouCanBookMe because people pay because one double booking or missed invite can cost more than years of subscription fees. The recurring cost buys OAuth refresh, webhooks, timezone databases, race conditions, reminders, deliverability, privacy, and uptime, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Cal.com
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source scheduling platform with calendar integrations and booking workflows.

alternatives.name: Cal.com Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited solo event types, calendars and bookings, with payments and notifications; team routing costs money.

facts.dataFormat: Account, availability, booking and integration records live in Cal.com's cloud and in the connected calendar, conferencing and payment providers
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan is solo-only; shared routing, round-robin scheduling and team administration cost extra.

alternatives.name: Calendly Free
alternatives.desc: One active event type and unlimited bookings; meeting polls survive, workflows and teams do not.

facts.dataFormat: Account, booking and calendar-integration records live in Calendly's cloud and connected calendar or conferencing providers
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan permits only one event type and one calendar and omits payments and automated reminders.

alternatives.name: Koalendar Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited booking pages and two calendar connections; payments, forms, reminders and team routing are paid.

facts.dataFormat: Account, booking and availability records live in Koalendar's cloud and connected calendar or conferencing providers
facts.gapVsPaid: Payments, booking-form questions, custom reminders, group sessions and team routing are paid features.

alternatives.name: TidyCal Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited one-person booking types and paid bookings on one calendar; group meetings and fancy emails cost extra.

facts.dataFormat: Account, connected-calendar, appointment and payment-integration records live in TidyCal and AppSumo's cloud services
facts.gapVsPaid: It connects one calendar and omits custom intake questions, advanced reminders, polls and approval workflows on the free plan.

alternatives.name: zcal Free
alternatives.desc: Unlimited links and calendars, custom questions, email reminders and Stripe payments; teams are paid and zcal takes 3%.

facts.dataFormat: Account and booking records live in zcal's cloud; Stripe processes and stores payment details for paid bookings
facts.gapVsPaid: Team scheduling is paid and zcal takes a 3% commission on Stripe payments.

alternatives.name: Zoho Bookings Free
alternatives.desc: A real one-person booking desk with forms, reminders and two-way sync; staff and payment plumbing cost extra.

facts.dataFormat: Account, booking and customer records live in Zoho's data centres and are synchronized with connected calendar and meeting providers
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan offers one service and no payments and is less flexible for custom booking-page and polling workflows.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Individual plan and a single-user booking service DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for YouCanBookMe in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, Google Calendar OAuth, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: read one calendar, publish booking pages with availability rules, create conflict-safe bookings, support rescheduling, and send confirmations and reminders.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement one account with configurable working hours, buffers, minimum notice, and booking horizon.
Connect Google Calendar using OAuth and store refresh tokens encrypted at rest.
Calculate availability in UTC and render it in the visitor's detected timezone.
Reserve slots transactionally, create calendar events, and prevent concurrent double booking.
Send confirmation, cancellation, and reminder email with signed management links.
Add an admin booking list, event-type editor, audit log, and calendar reconnect flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out Microsoft and Apple calendar support.
Deliberately leave out team round-robin routing.
Deliberately leave out payments, CRM workflows, and enterprise controls.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
